additional_info.subject: Description:
additional_info.body:
Hello,
Today a global outage on Cloudflare services, which eCarup relies to, impacted our ability to charge our vehicule.
Would it be possible to have the following backup solutions :
Charge with a locally defined PIN code
Provision local RFID card authentication
Provision local Vehicule ID authentification
Thank you for your help.
Also, if we can manage this directly by ourselves, either through any online platform, or through LAN acesss to the charging station, that would be great.
Best Regards,
Valentin

additional_info.body:
Dear Mr Harun Ar Rashid,
Thank you for your answer.
The idea would be to have both methods.
We would like to keep the OCPP backend to eCarUp for reporting purposes and central management of our charging stations and RFID cards.
But we don't have any access to the management portal of this particular charging station, either on a cloud platform, or on direct LAN (http/s aren't responding, but ping yes).
Note that the charging station has also a SIM card configured for internet connectivity through mobile network 4/5G, as the Siemens collaborator who installed it, says it was necessary to establish communication to cloud services (OCPP and Siemens platform).
Thanks for help.
Best Regards,
Valentin

additional_info.subject: RE: Fwd: ID0462572-DC/Si-D/CH-[RVP / T6 170004833] Ability to charge offline CRM:02681001111
additional_info.body:
Dear Valentin,
Thank you for reaching out regarding the configuration of local authentication methods for your charge points. We understand the importance of flexible and reliable authorization options, especially for ensuring seamless charging experiences.
We would like to provide clarity on setting up local authentication for PIN codes, RFID cards, and Vehicle IDs.
Understanding PIN Code Authorization for Offline Scenarios:
Regarding the ability to charge with a locally defined PIN code in an offline scenario, it's important to note that standard PIN authorization typically involves validation by the central OCPP Backend for security and centralized management. This means that for a PIN to be authenticated, the charge point generally needs to communicate with the backend. Therefore, a purely local PIN authorization without any backend involvement is not a standard feature in OCPP 1.6 and would not be possible for truly offline charging where no network connection is available.
Enabling Local RFID Card and Vehicle ID Authentication:
For local RFID card and Vehicle ID authentication, your charge points can indeed be configured to use a
Local Authorization List
. This list stores authorized identifiers directly on the charge point, allowing for quicker pre-authorization, even if there's a delay in communication with the central system.
To enable and manage this functionality, your OCPP backend provider will need to configure specific parameters on your charge points and manage the content of the Local Authorization List.
Required OCPP Parameters for Your Backend Provider:
To facilitate local pre-authorization for RFID cards and Vehicle IDs, we recommend requesting your OCPP backend provider to adjust the following parameters:
LocalAuthListEnabled
Recommended Value:
True
Purpose:
This parameter activates the charge point's internal local authorization list, allowing it to store and use authorized identifiers.
AuthorizeRemote
Recommended Value:
True
Purpose:
When set to
True
, the charge point will still send an
Authorize.req
message to the central system even if the user is authorized locally. This ensures that your central system remains aware of all transactions for logging, billing, and further validation, while still benefiting from local pre-authorization speed.
LocalPreAuthorize
Recommended Value:
True
Purpose:
In conjunction with
AuthorizeRemote
set to
True
, this parameter allows the charge point to immediately authorize a transaction if the
idTag
is found in its local list, without waiting for the central system's response. This significantly improves the user experience by reducing wait times.
LocalAuthListMaxLength
Type:
Integer
Purpose:
This defines the maximum number of entries (e.g., unique RFID tags or Vehicle IDs) that the local authorization list can hold.
Recommended Value:
Please discuss with your backend provider to set this to a number that adequately accommodates the local users you anticipate.
Action Required:
Please forward these parameter change requests to your OCPP backend provider. They have full control over these settings and are responsible for provisioning the actual RFID tags and Vehicle IDs into the Local Authorization List via the
SendLocalList.req
message.
Based on this comprehensive information, we will proceed to close this support ticket. Should you have any further questions or require assistance on new topics, please do not hesitate to open a new ticket.
Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.
With best regards,
Joao Francisco Louro Cardoso
Siemens S.A.

2845-547 Corroios, Portugal

additional_info.subject: Re: Fwd: ID0462572-DC/Si-D/CH-[RVP / T6 170004833] Ability to charge offline CRM:02681001111
additional_info.body:
Dear Joao,
Thank you so much for your reply.
As we have control over the OCPP backend (ecarup), I've already checked the following keys :
LocalAuthListEnabled is already set to true
AuthorizeRemote (not found), but AuthorizeRemoteTxRequests was found, with a value of false.
LocalPreAuthorize is set to false.
LocalAuthListMaxLength is set to 100
I've checked also on another Charging Station we own (Etrel) where the "offline mode" works, I have the following values :
LocalAuthListEnabled : True
AuthorizeRemoteTxRequests : False
LocalPreAuthorize : True
LocalAuthListMaxLength : 5000
I can definitively set the right values for most keys, just wanted to be sure regarding the 2nd key (AuthorizeRemote vs AuthorizeRemoteTxRequests).
Thank you for your feedback.
Best Regards,
Valentin
